elements.element: Services are warranted to be performed in a professional and workmanlike manner.
elements.evidence: Inserted sentence: "for thirty (30) days following performance, the Services will have been performed in a professional and workmanlike manner"; § 1(b) also contains a professional-and-workmanlike performance covenant.

elements.element: Deliverables or software are warranted to conform to their documentation.
elements.evidence: Inserted: "any software or other deliverable provided hereunder will conform in all material respects to its documentation".

elements.element: The software conformance warranty lasts 12 months.
elements.evidence: The inserted conformance period is "ninety (90) days following delivery", not twelve months; to reach preferred the drafter must state twelve (12) months for software.
The inserted Services warranty runs "for thirty (30) days following performance", short of the 90-day preferred period.

elements.element: Warranty remedies include repair or replacement.
elements.evidence: Inserted: "at Contractor's option, repair or replacement of the non-conforming software, deliverable or Services".
Inserted: "or a refund of the fees paid for them".

elements.element: Vendor warrants compliance with applicable laws.
elements.evidence: Retained § 5(a): Contractor warrants that its performance of the Services "to its knowledge, does not and shall not violate any applicable law, rule, or regulation" — a compliance warranty exists, though knowledge-qualified (a sub-element short of the unqualified preferred wording).

elements.element: Vendor warrants that the Services and Deliverables contain no malicious code.
elements.evidence: No malicious-code / virus warranty appears anywhere in § 5 or in the inserted paragraph; the drafter would need to add an express no-malicious-code warranty to reach preferred.

elements.element: Software is warranted to conform to its documentation for at least 90 days.
elements.evidence: Inserted: "for ninety (90) days following delivery, any software or other deliverable provided hereunder will conform in all material respects to its documentation" — meets the 90-day floor.

elements.element: Services are warranted for at least 30 days.
elements.evidence: Inserted: "for thirty (30) days following performance, the Services will have been performed in a professional and workmanlike manner" — an express, time-bounded Services warranty at the 30-day floor.

elements.element: Warranty remedies include repair or replacement.
elements.evidence: Inserted remedy sentence expressly provides "repair or replacement of the non-conforming software, deliverable or Services".
Inserted remedy sentence expressly provides "a refund of the fees paid for them".

reasons: The redline is position-complete at the fallback level: all four fallback elements (90-day software/deliverable conformance to documentation, 30-day Services warranty, repair-or-replacement, refund) are carried by operative inserted language rather than by the margin comment.

Preferred is not reached on three elements: the software period is 90 days rather than 12 months, the Services period is 30 days rather than 90 days, and there is no malicious-code warranty. These are period/scope gaps only, consistent with a deliberate fallback insert.
Compliance-with-law is satisfied by retained § 5(a), albeit knowledge-qualified; that is a sub-element shortfall to note in the rationale, not a separate defect to repair.

Minimality holds: a single concise insertion for a warranty gap, tracking the model remedy sentence, with no survival tail, no at-own-expense wording, no added damages categories or procedures, and no deletions elsewhere. The retained § 5(e) disclaimer is limited to implied warranties and expressly preserves express warranties, so no carve-out edit was needed and none was made.
No impermissible duplication: § 1(b) is a performance covenant without period or remedy, so the new time-bounded Services warranty with a stated remedy is necessary rather than redundant.

Intent is preserved: acceptance mechanics in § 4, the § 5(a)/(c) warranties and the § 5(e) disclaimer all survive without contradiction, and the insertion creates no undefined term or dangling cross-reference ("Services", "deliverable", "documentation" and "fees paid" all sit within existing defined structure).
Minor drafting nit for the drafter, not a defect: the remedy is "at Contractor's option", which mirrors the playbook model language but leaves election with the Vendor.
